fundamentals.pe_assessment: Provider-reported trailing P/E is 29.58 and forward P/E 25.98 at a close of MYR 7.69 (2026-11-11); provider market cap is MYR 67.95b. These are provider current-metadata figures only. The deterministic same-basis P/E could not be computed: share_basis is null on the quarterly EPS records, so no authenticated TTM EPS exists (the 2025-03-31 and 2025-06-30 quarters also lack usable EPS). Inference: a roughly 26-30x multiple is demanding against single-digit net margins, but no sector average is available and none is assumed. Valuation is an evidence gap, not a negative finding.
fundamentals.margin_analysis: Latest quarter (Apr-Jun 2026, ended 2026-06-30): gross margin 72.3%, operating margin 15.2%, net margin 8.1% (net income MYR 573m on revenue MYR 7,046m). The year-ago quarter (ended 2025-06-30) was 71.2% / 14.2% / 7.0%, so operating and net margins are higher year on year, comparable-period basis. Quarterly net margin over the last six periods ranged about 7.0%-9.4% with no clean trend. Inference: margins are improving modestly but stay within a stable band.
fundamentals.debt_analysis: Reported total debt (debt_scope=reported_total) is MYR 15,181m against total equity of MYR 31,305m at 2026-06-30, a debt-to-equity ratio of about 0.48 (computed). Debt was broadly flat across the last five balance sheets (MYR 15.15b-15.54b) while equity rose from MYR 30.46b (Jun 2025) to MYR 31.31b. Quarterly free cash flow was MYR 610m in the latest quarter but volatile: 181m, 965m, 586m, 173m, 610m across the last five quarters. Context from the prior pipeline briefing (2026-10-07, not independently verified here): H1 cash was only RM141m after finance and lease costs, which is a caution on cash conversion. Interest cover cannot be computed from the supplied data.
fundamentals.growth_outlook: Comparable-quarter growth (Apr-Jun 2026 vs Apr-Jun 2025): revenue +11.9% (MYR 7,046m vs 6,298m) and net income +29.3% (MYR 573m vs 443m). This is one comparable year-ago pair, so it is not a multi-period trend. EPS growth cannot be assessed (no year-ago diluted EPS); latest quarterly diluted EPS is MYR 0.0648 and is not annualized. Per the prior briefing (not verified here), H1 ex-exceptional profit was up about 22%. External context supplied with the task (unverified): Phillip Capital Buy, TP RM11.03, with 2H26 earnings expected higher; news found nothing newer than May 2026. The 3Q26 result is not yet released (expected late Nov 2026), so the latest statement is 134 days old as of the cutoff. Analyst consensus counts are 5 strong buy, 17 buy, 0 hold, 0 sell, 0 strong sell, up from 16 buy and 2 hold three months ago.
key_risks: Valuation is demanding on provider figures (trailing P/E about 29.6, forward about 26.0) and cannot be confirmed on a same-basis EPS; the thesis relies on continued earnings growth.
Weak cash conversion: quarterly free cash flow is volatile (MYR 173m-965m over five quarters), and the prior briefing noted only RM141m H1 cash after finance and lease costs (unverified here).
Financial evidence is stale for the cutoff: latest statement ended 2026-06-30 (134 days old) and 3Q26 results are not yet released, so a near-term print could change the picture either way.
Total debt of about MYR 15.2b is sizable, although leverage is moderate (about 0.48x equity) and has been flat.
Evidence gaps: no filing text index exists, so no management-stated principal risks could be cited; this is a data limitation, not evidence of absence of risk.
Price is below the 20, 50 and 200-day moving averages with RSI 25.5, which is a technical matter outside fundamentals but signals the market is not currently rewarding the earnings improvement.
key_strengths: Comparable-quarter earnings momentum: net income +29.3% and revenue +11.9% year on year in Apr-Jun 2026.
High gross margin of 72.3% with operating margin up from 14.2% to 15.2% year on year.
Moderate leverage: total debt about 0.48x equity, with equity growing across the last five reported balance sheets.
Strong sell-side positioning: 22 of 22 recommendations are buy or strong buy, with no holds or sells.
Low beta (0.156, provider-reported), consistent with a defensive healthcare operator.
fundamentals.summary: Operating fundamentals are improving (Apr-Jun 2026 revenue +11.9%, net income +29.3% year on year, margins higher, debt about 0.48x equity), but valuation rests on provider-reported P/E of about 29.6 that could not be verified on a same-basis EPS, and cash conversion is uneven. With no filing evidence, a 134-day-old statement and 3Q26 results pending in late November, neutral is the appropriate signal at medium confidence.

macro.fed_impact: Fed held the funds target at 3.75%-4.00% on 28 Oct 2026 (10-2 vote, two dissenters preferred a hike) after a 25bp hike on 16 Sep; the bias is hawkish. Higher USD rates raise global discount rates for long-duration defensive equities like IHH, but the effect on a low-beta (0.16) MYR-listed hospital operator is indirect. Source is secondary reporting (the Fed release text was not retrievable); no FRED macro_snapshot was available.
macro.interest_rate_outlook: BNM held OPR at 2.75% on 5 Nov 2026 (eighth straight hold; unchanged since the July 2025 cut). It sees 2026 GDP growth above 5%, and several houses (CIMB, Apex) expect a 25bp hike to 3.00% in 1H27. Malaysian rates are therefore flat now with a mild upward bias, a modest headwind to valuation (PE ~29.6x trailing, ~26x forward) and to the cost of IHH's MYR 15.2bn debt (a mix of currencies). Turkey's CBRT cut its policy rate 100bp to 36% on 22 Oct (CPI 29.77% in Oct, slightly above forecast), so further cuts are uncertain. The RBI hiked 25bp to 5.50% in Oct 2026. Rates are mixed across IHH's markets with no clear net direction.
macro.fx_impact: IHH reports in MYR but earns heavily in SGD, TRY and INR, so translation effects matter. USD/MYR ~4.06 (4 Nov close 4.0610/0660) and the ringgit firmed after the BNM hold. SGD/MYR ~3.166 on 6 Nov, with the ringgit slightly stronger versus SGD, a small translation drag on Singapore earnings (Gleneagles, Mount Elizabeth). The lira keeps depreciating structurally (market survey year-end USD/TRY ~51.6) with inflation near 30%, which erodes MYR-translated Acibadem earnings, though hyperinflation-adjusted pricing partly offsets this. The rupee is near record lows (~96.4-96.8 per USD in early Oct, close to 97), so Fortis contributions translate weaker. A firm MYR is a net translation headwind. No dated spot quotes for TRY or INR in November were found, so those levels are unverified.
sector_macro_factors: Healthcare is defensive and low-beta; demand is largely insensitive to the rate cycle and to GDP growth above 5% in Malaysia.
Malaysia's strong domestic growth and a firm ringgit support local volumes but depress MYR-translated foreign earnings.
Turkish medical inflation near 30% supports nominal Acibadem revenue, but TRY depreciation limits MYR-reported growth.
Hawkish Fed plus a possible BNM hike in 1H27 pressure rich healthcare multiples (PE ~26-30x).
geopolitical_risks: The Iran-war-related oil shock and foreign outflows pressure the INR and EM currencies (per RBI and rupee reporting).
Turkish reserve drawdown (net reserves ex-swaps ~USD 39bn, down ~USD 4.9bn in the week of 22 Oct) is a lira stability risk.
Global risk-off episodes (e.g. 6 Nov) weakened the ringgit against USD.
macro.summary: No FRED macro_snapshot was available. This view rests on dated web sources checked 2026-11-11: BNM OPR 2.75% (held 5 Nov), Fed 3.75-4.00% (held 28 Oct, hawkish dissent), USD/MYR ~4.06, SGD/MYR ~3.17, CBRT 36%, Turkish CPI 29.8%, RBI 5.50%. Macro forces are offsetting (defensive sector and strong Malaysian growth against a firm MYR, weak TRY and INR translation, and rich multiples facing hawkish rates), so the signal is neutral with low confidence.
